question: An airplane flying at a height of 300 m notices the angles of depression to two boats located on opposite sides as 45° and 30°. Find the distance between the two boats.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For an object at height h, if angles of depression to two points on opposite sides are α and β:

Total distance = h × (cot α + cot β)

Here, h = 300 m, α = 45° and β = 30°

Distance = 300 × (cot 45° + cot 30°)

Distance = 300 × (1 + √3) = 300(√3 + 1) m

**∴ The correct answer is 300(√3 + 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Height of airplane (AD) = 300 m

⇒ Angle of depression of Boat 1 (∠B) = 45°

⇒ Angle of depression of Boat 2 (∠C) = 30°

**Formula Used:**

⇒ tan θ = Perpendicular / Base

**Calculations:**

⇒ In right-angled ΔADB, tan 45° = AD / BD

⇒ 1 = 300 / BD

⇒ BD = 300 m

⇒ In right-angled ΔADC, tan 30° = AD / DC

⇒ 1 / √3 = 300 / DC

⇒ DC = 300√3 m

⇒ Total distance between the boats (BC) = BD + DC

⇒ BC = 300 + 300√3 = 300(√3 + 1) m

**∴ The correct answer is 300(√3 + 1) m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Same Side vs Opposite Sides

If two objects are located on the same side of the observer, the distance between them is h × |cot α − cot β|.

Angle of Elevation & Depression

The angle of elevation from an object to an observer is always mathematically equal to the angle of depression from the observer to the object due to alternate interior angles.
